items.stem: A contract call reverts but the user is still charged. Why?

options.text: Gas is consumed by the executed computation up to the revert, so the work is paid for
options.rationale: Correct: gas pays for execution even when the final state change is undone.

options.text: The network refunds all gas on any revert
options.rationale: Only unused gas is returned, not gas already spent.
Reverts consume the gas used before the failure.
Miners do not reimburse reverted gas.

items.explanation: Correct: gas pays for execution even when the final state change is undone.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about EIP-1559 are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The base fee is algorithmically adjusted per block based on demand
options.rationale: Correct: the base fee rises and falls with block fullness.

options.text: The base fee is burned rather than paid to the validator
options.rationale: Correct: burning the base fee is a defining EIP-1559 feature.

options.text: Users can no longer set any tip for validators
options.rationale: Users still set a priority fee (tip).

items.explanation: Correct: the base fee rises and falls with block fullness.

items.stem: What distinguishes a contract account from an externally owned account on Ethereum?

options.text: A contract account has associated code executed when it receives a message
options.rationale: Correct: contract accounts hold code; EOAs do not.

options.text: A contract account is controlled by a private key
options.rationale: That describes an EOA, not a contract account.

options.text: A contract account cannot hold a balance
A contract account has no address

items.explanation: Correct: contract accounts hold code; EOAs do not.
